title: Insulation Rebates in Burnaby 2026: Up to $5,500 from BC Hydro
desc: Over half of Burnaby households live in apartments, but 9,220 own an older house that can qualify. BC Hydro's insulation formula, a worked example and who is excluded.
lead: Burnaby is a city of towers and townhomes with older houses on its slopes. The insulation rebate fits that second group, so the first question is which one you live in.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for insulation in Burnaby
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's page on October 2, 2026. These amounts apply to owned houses heated mainly by electricity. Gas-heated houses should check FortisBC.

cards.title: Attic
cards.amount: $0.02 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Up to $900, with at least R12 added.

cards.title: Wall and basement areas
cards.amount: $0.09 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Up to $1,200 each for wall cavities, sheathing, and basement or crawlspace.

cards.title: Other areas
cards.amount: $0.07 x R added x sq ft
cards.note: Up to $1,000, with at least R20 added.

cards.title: Bonus for more than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro's page names the bonus but not the formula.

cards.title: Lower-income households
cards.note: Free evaluation and upgrades for income-qualified customers.

after_cards:
A sloped-lot example

A house on one of Burnaby's slopes may have a walk-out basement. Adding R-12 to 700 square feet of basement wall pays 0.09 x 12 x 700 = $756. Adding R-30 to a 1,000 square foot attic pays 0.02 x 30 x 1,000 = $600. Together that is $1,356, before any multi-upgrade bonus. Your invoice decides the final figure.
sections: Who in Burnaby can use this

The 2021 Census counted 101,135 households in Burnaby. Of those, 35,865 (35%) live in homes built before 1981, but 53% of Burnaby households are in apartments and 40% rent. Only 9,220 are owner-occupied single-detached houses from before 1981. If you are one of them, the rebate fits well. If you own a unit in a tower or townhouse complex, the Home Renovation Rebate does not apply. BC Hydro runs a separate Condo and Apartment Rebate Program for you.
A mild climate with a damp edge

Burnaby's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 1.1°C, and the coldest day was -16.2°C. Winters are not harsh, so insulation is as much about comfort and moisture control as the bill. Do not seal and insulate a damp crawlspace without a plan for ventilation. Ask your contractor how they will handle air sealing, because BC Hydro asks that insulation follow its best-practice guide for air sealing and insulation retrofits.
Where to put the money first

The wall and basement lines pay $0.09 per R per square foot, over four times the attic rate, but walls can cost more to open up. Ask for a separate price for each area so you can see the rebate against the cost line by line.

• A Home Performance Contractor Network member must install the insulation.
  • Only new material counts, and pest problems must be fixed first.
  • Insulation needed for a permitted addition does not qualify.
  • You have six months from the invoice date to apply.

claim_steps: Confirm you own a house, row home or duplex and that your heat is mainly electric.
Ask each contractor for a line-by-line price and the R-value added for each area.
After the job, check the invoice lists the insulation type, R-value and area.
If you are adding a second upgrade such as a heat pump, apply together.
faq: I own a townhouse in Burnaby. Can I use this rebate?

Possibly. BC Hydro accepts side-by-side row homes and townhouses when each unit has its own meter and the utility account is not in a strata corporation's name. Condos and apartments use a different program.
Which part of the house gives the most rebate?
Walls and basements pay $0.09 per R per square foot, against $0.02 for attics. The caps are $1,200 and $900.
Do I need an air sealing step?
BC Hydro requires that insulation follow its best-practice guide for air sealing and insulation retrofits.
Will insulation change my Burnaby bill much?
BC Hydro says it can save at least 10% of a home's energy cost. Burnaby's mild winters make the savings smaller than in the Interior.
Yes. Lower-income BC Hydro customers can apply for free evaluations and upgrades.
